label: Solar Priority
info:
Automatically powers AC loads from solar instead of shore power when the panels can carry them,
with as close to zero energy cycled through the battery as possible (storage mode, ~60% SOC).

Available solar capacity is MEASURED, not modelled: whenever an MPPT reports
/MppOperationMode == 2 (tracker active = unthrottled) its /Yield/Power IS its current
capacity. Probes by disconnecting shore for 90s (the MPPTs take ~40s to wake after the
shore drop — measured), then judges health on BATTERY POWER: solar mode is only kept
while the pack is not discharging (charging is fine). Big loads reconnect shore within
seconds.

If the pack sits ABOVE the target charge voltage (Max Charge lowered), the flow
BURNS the surplus into the loads — shore off, no sun required — then hands over to
solar or reconnects when the surplus is spent.

When solar cannot carry the whole load its energy is still HARVESTED
(v4.0): the sun fills the 0.15V lead band below the target on shore, and
each time the band fills the flow burns it into the loads. Heater-class
loads (>= 1kW) SUSPEND to shore instantly and the flow resumes within
seconds of the load ending.

States: shore -> probe (90s MPPT ramp) -> solar -> shore
        shore -> burndown (surplus or harvest) -> solar | probe | shore
        solar/burndown -> suspend (heater on shore) -> resumed

Capacity is measured WITHOUT dropping shore, via the dbus-recbms solar
boost (v1.2.0): raising only the MPPTs above the Quattro's regulation
point makes them run unthrottled, which is the state where their output
IS their capacity. The BMS driver owns the request, clamps it against
live cell data and expires it after 120s, so it can never stick.
Since driver v1.3.0 a standing solar lead also commands the Quattro
0.15V below the target (its absorption overshoots its setpoint), so
the MPPTs always finish the charge at the true target.
Settings (enable, PV capacity) persist across reboots.
See SETUP comment node for configuration.

name: SETUP — read me after import
info:
After importing this flow:

1. Verify the six solar-charger input nodes point at your two MPPTs
   (pre-filled: solarcharger/278 = MPPT 100/20, solarcharger/279 = MPPT
   150/35 — this boat's chargers). Each charger has a PV Voltage,
   PV Power and MPPT Mode node.
2. Verify 'AC Input Control', 'AC Input Feedback' and 'AC Out Power'
   point at the Quattro (pre-filled with vebus/276).
3. Verify the four 'victron-input-system' nodes auto-discovered
   'Venus system' (AC Load, Battery SOC, Battery Power, Battery Voltage)
   and that 'BMS Target CVL' points at the REC-BMS (pre-filled
   battery/200, path /RecBms/TargetChargeVoltage — dbus-recbms >= 1.3.0;
   deploy the driver BEFORE this flow version).
4. Deploy. (InstanceRegistry pins the toggle/slider to instances 221/222.)
5. Check the 'PV Capacity' slider on VRM (Solar group): pre-set to 1800W
   (the array's observed 7-day peak was ~1750W). It is only a sanity
   ceiling on the estimate — the real capacity is measured live.
6. Toggle 'Solar Priority' ON via the VRM dashboard (Solar group).

FIRST RUN: expect up to 5 min cooldown after enabling, then a probe
(exploratory if no capacity has been measured yet). If the Quattro
refuses /Ac/Control/IgnoreAcIn1 the probe FAULT-locks for 1h and logs
an error — check the vebus service selection and firmware.

Shore is assumed on AC input 1. If yours lands on AC input 2, change the
'AC Input Control' path to /Ac/Control/IgnoreAcIn2 and change the two
'feed.v === 0' checks in the Decision Engine to 'feed.v === 1'.

SOLAR BOOST (needs dbus-recbms >= 1.2.0):
While on shore the flow asks the BMS driver to raise ONLY the solar
chargers above the Quattro, by writing volts to
/RecBms/SolarBoost/Request. The MPPTs then run unthrottled
(MppOperationMode 2) and their output IS their capacity, so the array
is measured with shore still connected and no battery cycling.

Measured 2026-08-19: with a shared CVL the Quattro wins the tie and
squeezes both MPPTs to 0 W (17 min at 0 W while it pushed 1.3 kW from
shore). Lowering the Quattro does not help -- it ignores
/BatteryOperationalLimits/MaxChargeVoltage in that range. Raising solar
by 0.2V brought both chargers to mode 2 in 43-45 s.

The driver refuses the request if any cell is high, the cell
temperatures are out of band, or there is too little margin over the
present pack voltage (with only ~0.05V of margin the MPPTs took 126 s
to reach 5 % of the step, which would make the reading meaningless).
It expires by itself after 120 s and is cleared on driver restart, so a
crash here cannot leave the bank charging high.

Compare battV against /RecBms/SolarBoost/EffectiveChargeVoltage, not
the raw CVL -- the engine already does, so a boost is not mistaken for
a surplus and does not arm burn-down.

SOLAR LEAD (dbus-recbms >= 1.3.0): the Quattro's absorption holds
+0.05..0.15V ABOVE its commanded CVL (measured 2026-08-19; SVS on, all
three meters agreeing to 10mV -- the bias is in its regulation, not a
sense error). The driver therefore commands the Quattro solar_lead_v
(0.15V) BELOW the target and raises only the MPPTs back up to it, so
the Quattro lands at or just under the calibrated equilibrium and the
MPPTs -- which regulate accurately -- always finish the top-off at the
true target. This flow reads that TARGET from
/RecBms/TargetChargeVoltage; /Info/MaxChargeVoltage is now the
Quattro's lowered command and is NOT what battV converges to. Side
effect: below the target only solar has charging headroom, so on shore
the MPPTs run unthrottled whenever the pack sits under target --
passive solar priority plus continuous capacity readings.

LEAD VERIFICATION (dbus-recbms >= 1.4.0): systemcalc applies the
SolarVoltageOffset ONLY while the GX access level is Superuser (Settings >
General > Access level), and it evaluates that once per systemcalc
process. The driver compares com.victronenergy.system
/Control/EffectiveChargeVoltage with what it expects; on a sustained
mismatch it publishes the full target, refuses boosts, raises the battery
InternalFailure alarm to WARNING and explains itself in /RecBms/LeadFault.
This flow subscribes to that string ('Lead Fault' node -> node.error in
the debug sidebar / log) and to /RecBms/SolarLead: while the lead is 0
harvest-and-burn is disabled (no band to harvest). Fix: set access level
to Superuser, then 'svc -t /service/dbus-systemcalc-py'; the fault clears
by itself within ~10 s.

OWNERSHIP: while the toggle is ON, this flow owns /Ac/Control/IgnoreAcIn1
and re-asserts it every 30s. Turn the toggle OFF before controlling that
path manually or from another automation.

PERSISTENCE: enable state and PV capacity are saved to
solar-priority-state.json (writable-dir discovery: $HOME/.node-red, then
$HOME, then /data) and restored ~6s after every deploy/reboot — the flow
resumes on its own after a marina power cut.

HOW IT DECIDES (v4.2, built against live bus measurements 2026-08-18/20):
- Victron services publish on CHANGE only: battery power / SOC / MPPT mode /
  ActiveInput can be silent for minutes-hours. Silence = unchanged, so all
  values are last-known-good; service LIVENESS is tracked via paths that
  provably jitter ~1/s (system: /Ac/Consumption/L1/Power, vebus:
  /Ac/Out/L1/P, each MPPT: /Yield/Power while producing). A dead system or
  vebus service forces shore.
- Capacity: per-charger capture when /MppOperationMode == 2 (unthrottled =
  output IS capacity), fully trusted 15 min, faded to zero by 90 min. The
  MPPTs bulk-charge unthrottled for hours most mornings, so fresh
  measurements are the norm. A failed probe is itself a measurement.
- Adaptive panel model (v3.4, per MPPT): while a charger is THROTTLED at
  the CVL ceiling but passing even a trickle (the DC loads provide one
  continuously under Prefer Renewable sustain), the panel voltage's
  distance below open-circuit voltage reveals how much current the panel
  COULD source (single-diode I-V curve), so capacity is estimated
  continuously without probing. Unthrottled operation (mode 2, including
  every probe) calibrates the model, so probes ADAPT it. Shallow-draw
  estimates count as lower bounds (can justify a probe, never skip one);
  a deep-draw estimate is trusted, and a trusted-dim reading on either
  array suppresses blind exploratory probes (same sky).
- Panel Voc (max of both chargers, readable even when idle) gates
  day/night (55V, plus MppOperationMode 0 = charger asleep) and allows an
  exploratory probe in strong PLATEAUED daylight (65V, and not while Voc
  is still climbing out of dawn) when neither a capture nor the model has
  any signal, the fully-pinned-at-Voc case where bright and dim are
  indistinguishable.
- Probes also wait for the charger to be QUIET (battP <= 100W):
  disconnecting AC mid-charge resets the Quattro's charge cycle, and with
  Prefer Renewable Energy that cycle must complete once before sustain
  activates.
- Probes are BOOST-ASSISTED (v3.5): in the steady state the pack sits AT
  the target voltage = the MPPT ceiling, so a bare probe starts with ~0V
  of margin and the chargers ramp glacially (measured 2026-08-20: 25W at
  60s into a probe vs 600W in ~60s under a 0.30V boost — full sun both
  times). Each probe requests the boost for its ramp and releases it on
  exit; if the driver refuses, the probe proceeds unassisted. The
  handover leaves the pack slightly ABOVE the target (the boost charged
  it), and the MPPTs throttle until that surplus drains into the loads —
  so the deficit/surge exits are deaf while battV > target, and the
  deficit exit additionally waits out a 90s settle window after entry
  while the chargers re-ramp from a small margin.
- The solar->shore DEFICIT exit judges the 90s rolling MEAN of battery
  power (v3.6): hovering at the ceiling the MPPTs regulate voltage with
  a margin-limited response and throttle-hunt around the demand, so the
  instantaneous battery power flips sign even when the array carries the
  load on average (measured: 1W from a 350W-capable array at 0.01V of
  margin). The 400W surge exit stays instantaneous. The probe's big-load
  kill and the burn-down calm handover are also average-based (v4.0).
- HARVEST-AND-BURN (v4.0): when capacity < load, solar is no longer
  wasted. On shore the lead gives the MPPTs headroom to fill the 0.15V
  band below the target; when the band is full (battV within 0.02V of
  target, charger quiet, daylight) the flow enters burn-down and feeds
  the stored solar into the loads, then lets the sun refill. Harvest
  re-arms only after battV dipped 0.10V under target and climbed back
  WITHOUT material charger power (during a solar climb PV roughly
  matches the charge power; a Quattro recharge has near-zero PV) — a
  shore-fed climb never arms, so shore energy is never round-tripped
  and nothing arms at night. ~1.2 kWh per burn, ~10-15 full-cycle
  equivalents per year: negligible NMC wear. Probes (direct solar
  carry, no round-trip loss) take precedence when capacity clears the
  bar; harvest is the weak-sun fallback.
- SUSPEND (v4.0): a load >= 1kW for 3s (the water heater) reconnects
  shore IMMEDIATELY from solar or burn-down — no cooldown, no backoff —
  and the flow resumes the previous state ~10s after the load returns
  to its pre-suspend 60s average (+200W). A suspend older than 20 min
  becomes a normal shore transition. The pre-suspend average is
  snapshotted when the big load first appears, so the heater itself
  never pollutes the baseline.
- CEILING-STALL BURN (v4.1): in solar mode the sun refills the band and
  the pack parks at the target, where the MPPTs have no voltage margin
  and carry only a trickle of the load. That averaged deficit, while
  battV is still within 0.05V of the target in daylight with shore
  present, rolls into a burn-down instead of a shore exit (no backoff):
  the loads open margin under the chargers and the calm handover returns
  to solar. The burn-down's bottom exit still falls back to probe/shore
  if the sun has really gone.
- Battery power is the health signal: solar mode is kept only while the
  pack is not discharging. Charging in solar mode is allowed — surplus
  charges the pack until DVCC/CVL caps it at the storage target.
- battV > CVL + 0.05V means the pack holds SURPLUS energy (target was
  lowered, or an over-charge): the flow enters BURN-DOWN — shore is
  dropped and the loads run from the surplus, no sun required. The MPPTs
  wake on their own once battV crosses under the CVL; if they end up
  carrying the load (battery no longer discharging for 15s) burn-down
  hands over to solar mode seamlessly, otherwise it reconnects shore when
  battV falls 0.15V below CVL for 30s (well past load-induced sag, so the
  exit cannot flap).
- Burn-down loop protection (added after observing a burn -> recharge ->
  burn cycle live: the Quattro OVERSHOOTS the CVL while re-absorbing after
  shore returns, 56.78V @ +471W vs CVL 56.65V): (1) voltage above CVL only
  counts as surplus while the charger is quiet (battP <= 100W); (2) a
  completed burn-down LATCHES — one burn per surplus event — and re-arms
  only when the CVL changes (Max Charge slider moved) or battV exceeds
  CVL + 0.25V (a genuine overcharge, above the overshoot band).
- Probing (as opposed to burning) is still blocked while battV > CVL —
  the MPPTs physically cannot produce there (observed live: a full probe
  with both chargers asleep at 56.78V vs CVL 56.65V). A probe whose
  chargers have not woken by 60s is aborted early for the same reason.

Tunable thresholds live at the top of the 'Decision Engine' function node:
  SOLAR_MARGIN (1.2)      — capacity must beat avg load by 20%
  MIN_EST_W (100)         — minimum estimate worth probing
  READY_MS (30s)          — conditions must hold this long before probing
  RAMP_MS (90s)           — probe ramp; MPPTs wake ~40s after the shore
                            drop (measured live 2026-08-18), full power ~60s
  EVAL_MS (15s)           — averaging window at the end of the ramp
  DISCHARGE_TOL_W (50)    — battery discharge below this = 'not cycling'
  LOAD_EXCEED_MS (15s)    — mean deficit must persist this long
  DEFICIT_AVG_MS (90s)    — battery-power averaging window for that exit
  SURGE_W (400) / SURGE_MS (3s) — big-load fast exit (instantaneous)
  COOLDOWN_MS (5min)      — min time between transitions
  BACKOFF_MAX_MS (60min)  — failed-probe exponential backoff cap
  HB_STALE_MS (20s)       — service heartbeat timeout
  CAP_FRESH_MS (15min) / CAP_ZERO_MS (90min) — capacity trust window
  VOC_DAY_V (55) / VOC_EXPLORE_V (65) — daylight gates
  VOC_RISE_V (1V/10min)   — Voc still climbing = dawn, no explore
  MDL_* (see engine)      — adaptive panel model tunables
  CVL_MARGIN_V (0.05V)    — battV above CVL by more = surplus -> burn-down
  WAKE_MS (60s)           — MPPTs must be tracking by then or probe aborts
  BURN_EXIT_DROP_V (0.15V) / BURN_EXIT_MS (30s) — burn-down exit
  BURN_CALM_MS (15s)      — no discharge in burn-down = solar handover
  SURPLUS_QUIET_W (100W)  — no burn entry while the charger is pushing
  BURN_REARM_V (0.25V)    — overcharge level that re-arms a latched burn
  HARVEST_ARM_V (0.02V) / REFILL_RESET_V (0.10V) — harvest band edges
  HARVEST_MIN_EVID (100W) — bootstrap harvest needs this much sun signal
  SUSPEND_LOAD_W (1kW) / SUSPEND_MS (3s) — heater-class suspend trigger
  SUSPEND_MAX_MS (20min)  — suspend cap, then a normal shore stay
  RESUME_DELTA_W (200W) / RESUME_MS (10s) — resume when load is back
  MIN_SOC (40%) / SOC_EMERGENCY (30%) / SOC_DRIFT_MAX (2%)

ANTI-FLIP-FLOP: 5 min cooldown between transitions; failed probes back off
5m -> 60m exponentially. Backoff is released early only on evidence:
capacity (measured or modelled) clearing the bar, a >= 30 min stable
solar stint, or a re-enable. Because a failed probe stores the measured
capacity AND calibrates the model, the estimate itself blocks re-probing
until conditions genuinely improve.
